To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

excluded volume must be adequately accounted for when inferring compactness and asphericity of disordered proteins from smFRET data, and that the smFRET data for Sic1 are consistent with a heterogeneous ensemble of conformations that is more compact and less aspherical than the ensemble predicted by conventional methods.

excluded volume must be accounted for to infer the structural properties of a protein conformational ensemble by smFRET and, when it is properly taken into account, smFRET data are consistent with the heterogeneous conformational ensembling of disordered proteins.

excluded volume is necessary for smFRET to infer the structural properties of disordered proteins, and smFRET data on Sic1 are inconsistent with homogeneously expanded and contracted conformational states but consistent with heterogeneous states allowed by our method.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the physical interpretation of smFRET data on disordered proteins.
a fundamental issue in smFRET data analysis, namely, whether the smFRET-inferenced ensemble of protein conformations can be adequately described by a Gaussian chain or by Sanchez theory.
the physical basis of smFRET interpretation and the role of excluded volume in smFRET analysis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

smFRET data for disordered proteins, in general, are not consistent with the conventional procedures that presume a Gaussian chain model, the mean-field Sanchez theory of excluded volume, or the homogeneously expanded/contracted conformational ensemble.
the smFRET data for Sic1 are incompatible with the assumed homogeneously expanded and/or contracted conformational ensemble in the conventional procedures.

smFRET data for disordered proteins are consistent with heterogeneous compact ensembles of proteins, but the data are incompatible with conventional methods of interpretation that assume homogeneous Gaussian or Sanchez polymer chains.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the excluded volume is a necessary ingredient in smFRET analysis for inferring the compactness and asphericity of disordered proteins.
an adequate account of excluded volume is necessary for inferring compactness and asphericity of disordered proteins by smFRET.
smFRET data alone cannot distinguish between heterogeneous and homogeneous ensembles.
The main takeaway from our work is that
smFRET-inferable structural information of disordered proteins depends sensitively on the choice of polymer models and the method of data inference.

smFRET data can be consistent with heterogeneous enclaves of conformational subensembles that are not compatible with conventional polymer theories, provided that these enclaves are adequately described by polymer models that incorporate excluded volume and other physical effects.
the excluded volume of proteins is a crucial determinant of the distribution of endto-end distances.
